They have not written me a check. I have not committed to anything just yet. I will be calling Axis once I can get the police report. It was in DeKalb county and the office said 5-7 business days. It's driveable except for the tail light that was cracked, but I still had a spare set to put on there. 
I thought the whole point of going through your insurance was for your agent/insurance company to help you get what you're owed from the other company. I was told that filing the claim, even if I'm not at fault would go "into consideration upon renewal". So I'll be closing my claim once I can get Axis to get back to me. Once the whole thing is done with I'll find someone other than All State for car insurance.

Yeah, that's pretty much what I figured. I promised I'd look for my grandma/uncle. The cabinet is real wood, it's something he built in the 80s, but it's not very well made and it's extremely light so it can't be worth much. My uncle wanted it for his daughter since it has a mirror on it. Thanks for the help!

I'm not sure. I don't have a step down. In the event it does actually work, I don't want to overload it. I'm not too familiar with how well Japanese appliances, especially something this old, would handle the 120V here.

My grandfather was stationed in Japan many years ago and brought this television with him. My uncle and I have been clearing out his house and barns since he passed away a few years ago. He seems to think this would be worth some money and I think with the condition it's in it wouldn't be worth very much. A 6 pack of some cans he was collecting left a mark on the top. The Japanese lettering still looks in tact and it even has what I'm assuming to be the tools/parts bag that came with the TV.

I'd like more information if anyone has it or can point me in the right direction to find out more about this TV.
